thread:
maria: Quick Q — where can I pull a per-route breakdown of 4xx vs 5xx spikes? Trying to tune alerts for timeouts vs overload during a canary rollout.

jake: Grafana has a 'Errors — per route' dashboard under Observability. Quick link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/errors-per-route (if you don't have perms, ping infra).

maria: I only see the generic service dashboard. Any specific panel name I should search for?

jake: Search 'errors_by_route' or go to Dashboards > Errors > 'By route / status code'. There are heatmaps and a timeseries split by status. Also a companion Datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/errors-overview

ankit: If you want raw queries, here's a useful Datadog metric to break down by route and code:```
sum:nginx.errors{env:prod}.as_count().by{route,status}
```That gives you counts; divide by requests to get rates.

lisa: For tuning alerts, consider normalizing by traffic. Example monitor (Datadog):```
(sum:nginx.errors{env:prod,code:5xx}.rollup(sum,60) / sum:nginx.requests{env:prod}.rollup(sum,60)) > 0.01
```This triggers on >1% 5xx over 5m. Adjust thresholds per service.

kevin: 502/504 usually indicate upstream timeouts (client->gateway->backend). Add a tag for upstream component when emitting errors so you can filter: `upstream:backend` or `upstream:cache`.

maria: Any tips to separate timeouts vs overload? Timeouts show up as elevated latency + 5xx codes, overload often has rising queue lengths and CPU.

ankit: Exactly. Watch these panels together: 95th latency, request queue depth, CPU, and backend error rate. If latency and queue depth spike before 5xx, likely overload. If backend latency is flat but gateway 504s spike, likely upstream timeouts.

lisa: Also exclude health-check traffic from denominator for alerting. Use `!path:/health` in the request tag filter.

maria: How do we handle canary noise? I want alerts but don't want pager storms.

jake: Two options: 1) Lower sensitivity for the canary service tag (short-term), or 2) Use anomaly detection monitors that compare to the service's baseline. For quick fixes we add a temporary mute on the monitor for the canary time window (use the Alerts page -> Mute).

maria: OK thanks — I found the Grafana panel. Adding the Datadog query to the runbook: https://wiki.redwood.company/runbooks/errors

maria: That'd be great, thanks.

jake: TL;DR — Grafana panel + Datadog query above. Normalize by requests, split by `route` and `status`, tag upstreams, and mute during canaries or lower sensitivity.
